text:
The Constitution is supreme: it sits at the top, and federal statutes and treaties rank below it, because any of them can be struck down if they conflict with it. Below those come federal administrative regulations, then state law (state constitutions, statutes, regulations), then local ordinances. The team note is wrong, since ratification and legislative votes don't let a statute or treaty override the Constitution. Under the Supremacy Clause, valid federal law overrides conflicting state law, and courts have the power to strike down laws that violate the Constitution.

CONFIDENCE: 97
